name: Gaurav Gogoi
role: Indian parliamentarian from Assam and Assam Pradesh Congress Committee president
summary: Gogoi advocates stronger climate regulation, indigenous land safeguards and democratic participation. His Assam leadership supports expanded health coverage and social assistance, while his own statements combine refugee protection with enforcement of Assam’s migration settlement and proposed criminal penalties for religious insults.

ban-cartels.rationale: In the no-confidence speech he objected that six companies hold large shares of ports, cement, steel, telecom and coal and asked what kind of competitive economy that was; he did not propose a specific law.

corporate-influence.rationale: He criticizes closed industry consultations that exclude safeguards for the public and poorer households.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He argued the amendment bills breach the Constitution's basic structure and Article 14 rights, i.e. that constitutional limits bind a parliamentary majority; he did not discuss courts as such.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: He criticised GST on school pencils, stationery, uniforms and temples and its roughly 100 rates as harassment and called for restructuring GST.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The campaign he leads proposes expanded women’s transfers and pensions for older people.

decide-locally.rationale: He demands Gram Sabha and autonomous-council consent instead of overriding local land governance.

democracy-best.rationale: He explicitly favors strengthening democracy and active citizens over treating people as obedient subjects.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: His bill identifies an escalating climate threat and proposes mandatory emissions reporting backed by national oversight.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He invokes constitutional equality and nondiscrimination guarantees to reject discriminatory citizenship legislation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He demands nondiscriminatory legal protection for refugees regardless of religion or origin.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: He demands tribal land transfers stop unless affected communities and their constitutional councils give informed consent.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: He defends Sixth Schedule autonomous councils and urges constitutional safeguards for indigenous areas.

no-business-privileges.rationale: He opposes corporations receiving constitutionally protected community lands through coercion and bypassed procedures.

open-borders.rationale: He defends Assam Accord citizenship controls and rejects extending its migration cut-off to 2014.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He favors active citizen decision-making and organizing through small groups beyond party structures.

population-transfer.rationale: His refugee proposal requires non-refoulement and voluntary repatriation rather than forced return to danger.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He insists carbon-market revenues protect vulnerable households rather than subsidize business as usual.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: His proposed punishment covers remarks against religions; no prohibition on practicing other faiths is established.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: His parliamentary question seeks further tea-worker wage increases after an inadequate interim increment.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He supports Assam’s 1971 migration cut-off while separately advocating humanitarian refugee protection; this is not a blanket ban on legal immigration.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He proposes compulsory environmental reporting, regulator supervision and penalties for companies’ noncompliance.

religious-nation.rationale: He argued that the Assam Accord was not drawn on religious lines, that the CAA upends this, and in the Waqf debate defined nationalism as respect for every religion; the Constitution's equality of faiths is his stated reference.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: He promises legislation imposing five years’ imprisonment for remarks against any religion.

return-lost-territory.rationale: In the Operation Sindoor debate he asked why the operation did not aim at Pakistan-occupied Kashmir ('if not now, when?'); machine captions of one speaker, so medium.

separated-powers.rationale: In his speech opposing the simultaneous-elections amendment bills he argued that the Constitution's basic structure balances executive, legislature and judiciary and that the bills give the President and Election Commission excessive power.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He calls for uniform rule of law rather than rule by a party or ideological organization.

strong-leader.rationale: He rejects top-down political command that silences dissent and produces unilateral decisions.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He defends citizens’ and party members’ rights to criticize and express different opinions.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His Assam campaign guarantees cashless health coverage up to 25 lakh rupees per family.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: He explicitly supports accommodation, food and sanitation protections for refugees.

widespread-small-property.rationale: His state program converts annual allotments into permanent ownership for ten lakh indigenous landholders.

women-suffrage.rationale: He demands immediate implementation of women’s representation in the national legislature.

notes:
Reviewed environmental work from 2022, 2025 tribal-land submission, refugee article, parliamentary wage question and 2024–26 interviews and state campaign. Downloaded bill, full 2025 parliamentary sitting and The Week interview; other full articles read through web. Researched across all ten themes and checked all 490 statements, including every remaining null. State guarantees are attributed because he led that state campaign, not merely from Congress membership; no national party platform or allies’ independent promises are imputed. Unconditional transfers to women do not establish basic income for every adult. Caste-census advocacy is recorded as context, not converted automatically into a racial doctrine. Refugee rights coexist with Assam-specific restrictions; the latter are not opposition to every form of immigration. His religious-insult penalty is retained alongside democratic commitments; equal protection of faiths is not abolition of blasphemy penalties. Nuclear security questions do not establish nuclear expansion policy, and officials’ answers are not his views. Personal allegations involving his wife and children do not establish ideological positions. Detailed monetary, trade, gender-identity, military and technological doctrines remain unknown. No inferred answers.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 6 answers taken from it, 4 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass. Read in full or by speaker: Lok Sabha debate texts of 2 Jul 2024, 31 Jul 2024, 8 Aug 2024 (Waqf introduction), 8 Aug 2023, 11 Dec 2024, 17 Dec 2024, 11 Mar 2025, 2 Apr 2025, 30 Jul 2025 and 8 Aug 2025, plus the Operation Sindoor video captions. Much of his speech time is attack on the government, which states no position on a statement; those are left null. His 28 Jul 2025, 3 Dec 2024, 8 Dec 2025, 10 Mar 2026 and 16 Apr 2026 sitting texts were not retrievable from sansad.in (HTTP 500). Searches for caste census/reservation, farm laws, privatisation, Gaza/Ukraine and UCC returned no statement of his own; his UCC remark (May 2026) only accuses the BJP of polarisation and takes no side on the code. Wikipedia and press paraphrase were used only to locate evidence.
